day_shape: 218 items: 27-nation UK-led Strait of Hormuz multinational mission statement republished twice, Iran-permitted Chinese and Japanese vessel transits, CENTCOM's Cooper says Iran's defence industry set back 90%, Araghchi works BRICS sidelines in New Delhi, heavy regime-channel volume.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz traffic and coalition
threads.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence republished a joint statement from 27 countries on the Multinational Military Mission for the Strait of Hormuz dated 12 May. Tehran-linked outlets reported Chinese and Japanese vessels transiting with Iranian permission, a Fujairah seizure incident, and an Iranian lawmaker proposing annual fees on Hormuz fibre-optic cables.

threads.label: BRICS New Delhi diplomacy
threads.summary: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi held sideline meetings with Russia's Lavrov, India's Ajit Doval and Thailand's foreign minister at the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting, telling delegates 'there is no military solution' on Iran. Iran International reported Araghchi accused the UAE of direct involvement in military operations against Iran during the session.

threads.label: US assessment of Iran's capabilities
threads.summary: CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said US bombings have dramatically reduced Iran's threat to neighbours and set back its defence industry by 90%, while saying Iran retains strike capability. IRIB countered by citing CNN and New York Times reporting that intelligence assessments show Iran preserved significant drone and coastal-missile capacity.

threads.label: Hezbollah-Israel northern front
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported three civilians wounded in a Hezbollah attack on northern Israel ahead of a third round of Israel-Lebanon talks, and IDF officials told ToI the Hezbollah drone threat was 'serious but blown out of proportion'. IRIB cited Israeli Channel 15 saying Hezbollah had introduced a new generation of suicide drones.

threads.label: Yemen prisoner exchange
threads.summary: The UN Secretary-General's spokesperson announced that after 14 weeks of negotiations in Amman the parties in Yemen agreed to release over 1,600 conflict-related detainees, the largest such deal since the war began. The Jerusalem Post reported the exchange would involve the internationally recognised Yemeni government and the Iran-backed Houthis.

threads.label: Domestic war-economy and crackdown measures
threads.summary: Iranian state outlets reported asset confiscations of dozens of alleged 'traitors' in Hamadan to fund war reconstruction, a 990-tonne hoarded-goods seizure in Tehran, extended debt-repayment relief for war-damaged firms, and reduced customs duties on medicine. Iran International reported lethal-force allegations during January Najafabad and Mashhad protests, including the death of 18-year-old Parham Mehrabi.

threads.label: Iranian retaliation rhetoric and parliament
threads.summary: Iran International reported a senior lawmaker saying parliament is reviewing a bill mandating a €50 million reward for killing President Trump in retaliation for the assassination of Iran's leader. Defa Press posted a 40-day commemoration for the assassinated armed forces commander Seyyed Abdolrahim Mousavi, and IRIB reported Iraqi crowds preparing for the 'martyred leader's' funeral.

Following the pursuit of the Chinese foreign minister and China's ambassador to Iran, facilitation of the transit of Chinese vessels was pursued on the basis of the deep relations between the two countries and strategic partnership, and it was finally agreed that a number of Chinese vessels, as requested by that country, would transit this area after agreement on Iran's Strait management protocols. events.title_en: Bloomberg: France's unemployment rate reached above 8 percent for the first time in five years
events.summary_en: Bloomberg: France's unemployment rate reached above 8 percent for the first time in five years. This figure dealt a severe blow to government promises regarding employment and is indicative of a slowdown in the labour market of Europe's second-largest economy. Reduced consumer demand and high interest rates have caused companies to refrain from hiring new staff and layoffs in industrial sectors have increased. According to a French statistics office report, unemployment among young people under 25 has grown at a faster rate and approached 18 percent.

events.title_en: Surveillance of Starlink users by the Zionist regime
events.summary_en: Surveillance of Starlink users by the Zionist regime. A Haaretz investigation shows that two Israeli companies, through developing technology, have been able to identify the location of Starlink users and in some cases their user information. These companies map the location of Starlink terminals worldwide and disclose the locations of those connecting to the internet through these devices. According to Haaretz, these companies can locate satellite communication devices, monitor the number of devices connected to each base station and identify users through their mobile phone numbers or associated social media accounts.

events.title_en: The Economist: America faces a new food price shock
events.summary_en: The Economist: America faces a new food price shock. Currently, the greatest pressure from the Iran war on US food prices is seen in two stages of food packaging and transport in the supply chain. A large portion of food packaging is plastic, which itself is produced from oil. Petrochemical raw materials have now become approximately 40 percent more expensive. Additionally, 80 to 90 percent of American food products are transported by truck. With rising fuel prices, getting food to shop shelves has become significantly more expensive and this process will continue.
